reasons: Prerequisite conflict: CS4224 requires CS3223, which requires CS2102. CS2102 requires CS2040S (completed) and CS1231/MA1100 (CS1231S is completed). However, CS3103 requires CS2105. CS2105 requires CS2040S (completed). The main issue is the sequence: Student wants CS4224 before CS3103. CS4224 needs CS3223. CS3223 needs CS2102. CS2102 needs CS1231 (met by CS1231S) and CS2040S (met). So CS2102 can be taken in Sem 3. Then CS3223 in Sem 4. Then CS4224 in Sem 5. But CS4224 is offered only in Sem 1. Sem 5 is Y3S1, which is Sem 1 of the academic year. So CS4224 can be taken in Sem 5. CS3103 is offered only in Sem 1. So CS3103 can be taken in Sem 5 or later. But CS3103 needs CS2105. CS2105 needs CS2040S. CS2105 can be taken in Sem 3. So CS3103 can be taken in Sem 5. The constraint 'CS4224 before CS3103' means Sem(4224) < Sem(3103). If both are in Sem 5, this is not strictly before. If 4224 is Sem 5, 3103 must be Sem 6 or later. 3103 is Sem 1 only. So 3103 can be Sem 7 (Y4S1) but student is on exchange. So 3103 cannot be taken after Sem 5 if 4224 is in Sem 5. If 4224 is Sem 3? No, 4224 needs 3223. 3223 needs 2102. 2102 needs 1231 and 2040S. 2102 can be Sem 3. 3223 Sem 4. 4224 Sem 5. 3103 Sem 7 (Exchange). Impossible. If 4224 is Sem 1? No, student is in Sem 3. So 4224 earliest Sem 5. 3103 earliest Sem 5. Cannot be strictly before. Thus no plan satisfies 'CS4224 before CS3103' given exchange in Y4S1 and offering constraints.
